[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Shell Scripting (Bash) in Linux System Administration"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Bash (Bourne Again Shell) scripting is a powerful tool for automating tasks in Linux system administration. It allows you to write scripts that can execute a series of commands, making it easier to manage systems, perform repetitive tasks, and create custom utilities."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Basic Script Structure"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Bash script typically starts with a shebang line, which specifies the interpreter to use for executing the script. This is usually '#!/bin/bash'. After the shebang, you can add comments to explain the script's purpose and functionality. The rest of the script consists of commands and control structures."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"#!/bin/bash
# This is a simple Bash script
echo "Hello, world!""},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Variables"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Variables are used to store data in Bash scripts. You can assign values to variables using the '=' operator. To access the value of a variable, you use the '$' symbol."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"name="John"
echo "Hello, $name!""},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Input and Output"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Bash scripts can interact with the user through standard input (stdin) and standard output (stdout). The 'read' command is used to read input from the user, and the 'echo' command is used to display output."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"echo "Enter your name:"
read name
echo "Hello, $name!""},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Conditional Statements"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Conditional statements allow you to execute different blocks of code based on certain conditions. The 'if', 'elif', and 'else' keywords are used to create conditional statements."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "No arguments provided"
elif [ $# -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "One argument provided: $1"
else
  echo "Multiple arguments provided"
fi"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Loops"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Loops allow you to repeat a block of code multiple times. Bash supports 'for' and 'while' loops."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  echo "Number: $i"
done

count=1
while [ $count -le 5 ]; do
  echo "Count: $count"
  count=$((count + 1))
done"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Functions"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Functions allow you to group a set of commands into a reusable block of code. You can define functions using the 'function' keyword or by simply writing the function name followed by parentheses."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"function greet {
  echo "Hello, $1!"
}

greet "Alice"
greet "Bob""},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Command Substitution"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Command substitution allows you to capture the output of a command and use it as a value in your script. You can use '$()' or backticks (`) for command substitution. However, using '$()' is generally preferred because it is more readable and can be nested."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"date_output=$(date)
echo "Current date and time: $date_output""},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Error Handling"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"Error handling is crucial for writing robust Bash scripts. You can use the 'set -e' command to make the script exit immediately if any command fails. You can also use 'try...catch' like constructs using conditional statements and checking the exit status of commands."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"set -e

mkdir my_directory
if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "Failed to create directory"
  exit 1
fi"},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Commonly Used Commands in Scripts"},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ls: List directory contents"},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"cd: Change directory"},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"mkdir: Create a directory"},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"rm: Remove files or directories"},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"cp: Copy files or directories"},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"mv: Move or rename files or directories"},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"grep: Search for patterns in files"},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"sed: Stream editor for text manipulation"},{"order":36,"type":"bullet_point","text":"awk: Pattern scanning and processing language"},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"find: Search for files in a directory hierarchy"},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"By mastering these concepts, you can write powerful and efficient Bash scripts to automate various tasks in Linux system administration."}]
